text:
michelle: Heads-up — FinServX (big SOC 2 customer) is asking we ship Console-only policy templates and a visual audit workflow before we open the API. They argue compliance teams need UI first. How do we want to sequence this vs an API-first approach?

aj: Oof — common ask. My gut: API-first + thin Console is fastest and preserves developer velocity. Console parity is expensive and gets stale.

santiago: +1 api-first. We can expose admin APIs and ship a lightweight Console wrapper for customers that really need UI. That avoids blocking all customers.

rachel: We should use RICE to make this concrete. Impact is high for FinServX revenue but effort for a full Console is also high.

elllen: (typo) ellen: Agree w/ Santiago. Also need launch criteria for both paths — what counts as "done" for FinServX vs platform customers.

michelle: Here's a quick RICE sketch that we can iterate on:
```
Option A - Console-first
Reach: 1 (FinServX only)
Impact: 8
Confidence: 6
Effort (months): 6
RICE score: (Reach*Impact*Confidence)/Effort = (1*8*6)/6 = 8

Option B - API-first + minimal Console
Reach: 4 (FinServ + 3 similar customers)
Impact: 6
Confidence: 7
Effort: 3
RICE score = (4*6*7)/3 = 56
```

aj: That math makes the tradeoff pretty clear. API-first wins hard on RICE since effort is lower and reach is broader.

santiago: Sequencing suggestion: 1) Publish admin APIs + docs 2) Ship a minimal Console view (template gallery + audit view) as a thin react wrapper 3) Iterate on UX if adoption justifies.

rachel: Agree. Add launch criteria: API-first path needs (a) documented API with examples, (b) RBAC keys + KMS integration, (c) end-to-end e2e test with one enterprise pilot, (d) SLA/latency baseline. For Console minimal: (a) view-only template gallery, (b) exportable audit CSV, (c) granular role mapping UI.

michelle: FinServX will push back on "view-only" — they want edit templates in UI. Can we scope an "enterprise edit" toggle behind a feature flag and a signed contract?

elllen: Yes — feature flag + access gating is fine. That keeps the main rollout API-first for everyone else.

triage-bot: NOTE: this thread mentioned an enterprise contract. Created ticket #PLAT-894 for "api-admin-templates + minimal console" and assigned to @aj.

aj: I'll pick up the ticket. Proposed timeline: API + RBAC + KMS + docs in 6 weeks for pilot; minimal console in 10 weeks behind FF.

santiago: Devs: can infra support the RBAC/KMS timeline?

aj: I'll sync w/ eng-infra tomorrow. If infra needs more time, we keep the API gated to a partner pilot and accelerate the thin console.

rachel: One more metric to include in launch criteria: time-to-onboard for admin users (target < 2 hours with docs + support). Also track number of edits via Console in first 30 days.

michelle: Good call. Final: move forward with API-first + thin Console. Offer FinServX an expedited pilot + feature-flagged edit capability under contract. I'll handle customer comms.

ellen: Action items: aj -> open design doc + schedule infra sync; santiago -> prototype thin Console components; michelle -> customer comm and contract clause; rachel -> finalize RICE sheet and metrics.

michelle: Thanks all. If anyone thinks this flips, call it out in next 24h, otherwise I'll file the roadmap update. :thumbsup:
